subject: Reserved capacity addendum — doubling reserved GPUs and revised per-hour pricing
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Reserved capacity addendum — proposal to double reserved GPUs

Hi Carlos / Aisha / Procurement team,

Quick update as we approach your renewal window on Dec 5: based on the throughput telemetry you shared (avg sustained load and peaks), we put together a proposal to move NovaHealth from 16 → 32 reserved GPUs in your dedicated pool. The main goals: reduce tail latency during peak inference, simplify capacity planning, and lower your per-token unit cost via a larger reserved commitment.

What we're proposing in the attached pricing packet (redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf):
- 32-GPU reserved pool, 12-month term (option for 24-month)
- Revised per-GPU-hour reserved rate with tiered discounts at 24/36 month commits
- Throughput guarantee: target baseline throughput and a 99.9% availability objective; we include a burst policy for short peaks

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm desired term (12 vs 24), 2) procurement sends PO/contract contact, 3) we align on a start date and a 30-day ramp plan to validate throughput and caching config.

Attaching the pricing packet and a lightweight SOW draft. Happy to jump on a short call early next week to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity addendum — proposal to double reserved GPUs

Thanks Dev.

We reviewed the packet with engineering and procurement. A few clarifying items before we lock term:
1) Can you provide the committed per-GPU-hour rate for 12- vs 24-month terms in a single table? We want line-of-sight into the blended hourly cost at 100% utilization vs our current blended (we're metricizing on average token throughput).
2) What exactly does your throughput guarantee cover? We need an SLA that maps to our customer-impact metrics (99.9% of requests under 300ms sampling latency) — is that achievable at 32 GPUs or do we need extra burst capacity?
3) Any enterprise procurement redlines we should expect in the addendum (data residency, audit logs retention, indemnity)?

Procurement: please advise if PO will come from NovaHealth US or EU legal entity — that will determine invoicing.

If you can get a short write-up + a slim pricing table (one pager) by Wednesday, we can get legal/procurement looped. Also request a usage snapshot for the last 60 days (we'll attach internally in our next note).

— Aisha
VP, Product Operations — NovaHealth

Subject: FW: Reserved capacity addendum — proposal to double reserved GPUs (pricing + SOW highlights)

Hi Aisha / Carlos — attaching the slim pricing table and SOW highlights (see attachments). Key points below:

Summary pricing (blended per-GPU-hour) — quoted as reserved GPU-hours:
- 12-month term, 32 GPUs reserved: $6.20 per GPU-hour blended at 85% utilization
- 24-month term, 32 GPUs reserved: $5.45 per GPU-hour blended at 85% utilization (3% lower at 100% utilization due to tier)
- We include a 10% one-time ramp credit to assist with on-boarding anomalies for the first 30 days (applies to invoices in first billing period).

Throughput guarantee (SLA draft language):
- Baseline throughput target: steady-state support for up to 220 concurrent inference streams (measured at the model entrypoint).
- Latency objective: 99.9% of requests under 300ms for configured models when input token length <= 512 and batch sizes <= our recommended settings.
- Availability: 99.9% platform availability for the reserved pool; for short multi-minute peaks we will allow automatic burst to a shared capacity tier up to an additional 6 GPUs (subject to available capacity).
- Fallback policy: if reserve pool cannot meet the SLA, we will transparently route to a compatible lower-cost variant and notify your on-call; credits are eligible if monthly availability < 99.9%.

Operational items included: daily token-level cost reporting, per-route latency histograms, and an initial 4-week verification period where we run joint validation tests. After validation we convert to production-only monitoring.

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf (updated), SOW_NovaHealth_Dedicated_32GPU.docx (SOW highlights), usage_snapshot_nov2026.csv (their last-60-day usage we requested).

If you confirm the term (12 vs 24) and the PO path, we can issue the addendum and a DocuSign envelope that contains the pricing addendum + SOW.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks Rishi / Dev.

We reviewed the pricing table and the SLA language with engineering and procurement. High level: we are supportive of moving to 32 GPUs on a 12-month term, subject to final SOW edits and procurement sign-off. A couple of asks before we sign:

1) Can NovaHealth get the 30-day ramp credit you proposed as an invoice-level credit (we prefer a line-item credit) — procurement wants this explicit in the addendum.
2) We want the availability SLA tied to our incident severity model (i.e., severity 1 incidents trigger the credit process). Please include an appendix mapping severity to credit levels.
3) Legal asked for a data-retention statement confirming audit logs retention for at least 12 months and that logs can be exported on request.

Procurement: we will route the PO from NovaHealth US (procure@novahealth.ai). Expect an initial PO number within 5 business days after the addendum is updated.

If you can update the addendum with the ramp credit as a line item and add the severity-credit mapping + logs retention clause, we can proceed to DocuSign. We may request a short phone call with legal to expedite.

Carlos Mendoza
Head of Platform Operations — NovaHealth
